title: Interactive Epidemic Curves with Plotly
text: geom_epicurve() function works seamlessly plotly create interactive epidemic curves custom tooltips. vignette demonstrates: Basic interactivity: Converting static plots interactive visualisations Custom tooltips: HTML-formatted hover information Time periods: Hourly, daily, weekly epidemic curves Large outbreaks: Automatic column chart mode tooltips Symbols: Using Unicode symbols emoji interactivity Annotations: Adding timeline context (best static plots) Simply create plot ggplot2 convert using ggplotly().

title: Interactive Epidemic Curves with Plotly
text: First, let’s create basic interactive epidemic curve: Hover square see onset date. square represents one case, stacked vertically date!
code: library(paulmisc) library(ggplot2) library(plotly) #>  #> Attaching package: 'plotly' #> The following object is masked from 'package:ggplot2': #>  #>     last_plot #> The following object is masked from 'package:stats': #>  #>     filter #> The following object is masked from 'package:graphics': #>  #>     layout  # Generate example outbreak data cases <- simulate_outbreak(n = 50, seed = 123) # Create ggplot with text aesthetic for tooltips p <- ggplot(cases, aes(x = onset_date, text = format(onset_date, "%d %B %Y"))) +   geom_epicurve(fill = "steelblue") +   labs(     title = "Interactive Epidemic Curve",     x = "Date of Onset",     y = "Number of Cases"   ) +   theme_minimal()  # Convert to interactive plotly plot # tooltip = "text" shows only our custom tooltip ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text")

title: Interactive Epidemic Curves with Plotly
text: Now let’s colour age group add custom tooltips:
code:
# Add custom tooltip text (plain text format) cases$tooltip <- paste0(   "Case ", cases$case_id, "
",   "Date: ", format(cases$onset_date, "%d %B %Y"), "
",   "Age Group: ", cases$age_group, "
",   "Sex: ", cases$sex, "
",   "Setting: ", cases$setting, "
",   "Outcome: ", cases$outcome )  # Create plot with custom tooltips p <- ggplot(cases, aes(x = onset_date, fill = age_group, text = tooltip)) +   geom_epicurve() +   scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2", name = "Age Group") +   labs(     title = "Interactive Epidemic Curve by Age Group",     x = "Date of Onset",     y = "Number of Cases"   ) +   scale_y_epicurve() +   theme_minimal()  # Convert to interactive, showing only our custom tooltip ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text")

title: Interactive Epidemic Curves with Plotly
text: Interactive plots work faceting :
code: p <- ggplot(cases, aes(x = onset_date, fill = sex, text = tooltip)) +   geom_epicurve() +   scale_fill_manual(     values = c("Female" = "#D55E00", "Male" = "#0072B2"),     name = "Sex"   ) +   facet_wrap(~ setting, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +   labs(     title = "Interactive Epidemic Curves by Setting",     x = "Date of Onset",     y = "Number of Cases"   ) +   scale_y_epicurve() +   theme_minimal()  ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text")

title: Interactive Epidemic Curves with Plotly
text: complete control tooltip content. Use HTML formatting rich tooltips:
code:
# Create formatted tooltips with HTML cases$tooltip <- with(cases, paste0( "Case ", case_id, "
", "Date: ", format(onset_date, "%d %B %Y"), "
", "Demographics: ", age_group, ", ", sex, "
", "Setting: ", setting, "
", "Outcome: ", outcome )) p <- ggplot(cases, aes(x = onset_date, fill = outcome, text = tooltip)) + geom_epicurve() + scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Pastel1", name = "Outcome") + labs( title = "Interactive Epidemic Curve by Outcome", x = "Date of Onset", y = "Number of Cases" ) + scale_y_epicurve() + theme_minimal() ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text")

title: Interactive Epidemic Curves with Plotly
text: Epidemic curves work different time scales - ’s hourly outbreak: width automatically adjusts based time unit detected!
code:
# Create hourly outbreak data hourly_cases <- simulate_outbreak( n = 16, time_unit = "hourly", exposure = "2024-06-01", seed = 321 ) # Add tooltips with formatted time hourly_cases$tooltip <- paste0( "Case ", hourly_cases$case_id, "
", "Time: ", format(hourly_cases$onset_time, "%d %b %H:%M") ) p <- ggplot(hourly_cases, aes(x = onset_time, text = tooltip)) + geom_epicurve(fill = "darkred") + labs( title = "Hourly Epidemic Curve (Interactive)", x = "Time of Onset", y = "Number of Cases" ) + scale_y_epicurve() + theme_minimal() ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text")

title: Interactive Epidemic Curves with Plotly
text: large outbreaks, plot automatically switches column chart mode case counts exceed threshold:
code:
# Simulate a large continuous outbreak large_outbreak <- simulate_outbreak( n = 200, pattern = "continuous", date_range = 10, exposure = "2024-01-01", seed = 456 ) # Count cases per date for custom tooltips date_counts <- aggregate(case_id ~ onset_date, large_outbreak, length) names(date_counts)[2] <- "count" # Add tooltip text to each case large_outbreak <- merge(large_outbreak, date_counts, by = "onset_date") large_outbreak$tooltip <- with(large_outbreak, paste0( "Date: ", format(onset_date, "%d %b %Y"), "
", "Cases: ", count )) # Create plot with all cases (geom_epicurve needs one row per case) p <- ggplot(large_outbreak, aes(x = onset_date, text = tooltip)) + geom_epicurve(fill = "coral", max_stack = 20) + labs( title = "Large Outbreak (Column Chart Mode)", subtitle = "Auto-switched because some dates have >20 cases", x = "Date of Onset", y = "Number of Cases" ) + scale_y_epicurve() + theme_minimal() ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text")

title: Interactive Epidemic Curves with Plotly
text: Use custom symbols interactive tooltips:
code:
# Create smaller outbreak for symbols symbol_cases <- simulate_outbreak(n = 30, seed = 789) # Add detailed tooltips symbol_cases$tooltip <- with(symbol_cases, paste0( "🔴 Case ", case_id, "
", "Date: ", format(onset_date, "%d %B"), "
", "Age: ", age_group, "
", "Sex: ", sex )) p <- ggplot(symbol_cases, aes(x = onset_date, colour = sex, text = tooltip)) + geom_epicurve(symbol = "●", symbol_size = 6) + scale_colour_manual( values = c("Female" = "#D55E00", "Male" = "#0072B2"), name = "Sex" ) + guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(label = "●", size = 6))) + labs( title = "Interactive Epidemic Curve with Symbols", x = "Date of Onset", y = "Number of Cases" ) + scale_y_epicurve() + theme_minimal() ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text")

title: Interactive Epidemic Curves with Plotly
text: Timeline annotations work seamlessly plotly using code static plots: shaded period, event line, labels convert plotly automatically!
code:
# Add tooltip data cases$tooltip <- with(cases, paste0( "Case ID: ", case_id, "
", "Date: ", format(onset_date, "%d %b %Y"), "
", "Age: ", age_group )) # Create plot with annotations - same code works for both static and interactive! p <- ggplot(cases, aes(x = onset_date, text = tooltip)) + geom_epicurve(fill = "steelblue") + annotate_period( date = as.Date("2024-05-28"), end_date = as.Date("2024-06-02"), label = "Exposure period", fill = "yellow", alpha = 0.25 ) + annotate_event( date = as.Date("2024-06-05"), label = "Investigation", colour = "red" ) + labs( title = "Interactive Outbreak Timeline", subtitle = "Hover over cases for details", x = "Date", y = "Cases" ) + scale_y_epicurve() + theme_minimal() # Convert to plotly - all annotations transfer automatically! # ggplotly() doesn't render ggplot subtitles, so re-inject the title via # layout() using an HTML
+ for the subtitle. ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text") |> layout(title = list( text = paste0( "Interactive Outbreak Timeline", "
Hover over cases for details" ) ))

title: paulmisc: Epidemiological Visualization & SQL Tools
text: Simulate outbreaks different epidemiological characteristics adjusting incubation period parameters. meanlog parameter controls median incubation period (median = exp(meanlog) days), sdlog controls spread around median:
code: # Short incubation period (e.g., Salmonella, norovirus) # Median incubation: exp(0.5) ≈ 1.6 days short_incubation <- simulate_outbreak(   n = 100,   exposure = as.Date("2024-08-15"),   meanlog = 0.5,   sdlog = 0.3,   seed = 123 )  # Long incubation period (e.g., Hepatitis A) # Median incubation: exp(3) ≈ 20 days long_incubation <- simulate_outbreak(   n = 100,   exposure = as.Date("2024-08-15"),   meanlog = 3,   sdlog = 0.5,   seed = 123 )  # Compare side by side library(patchwork)  p1 <- ggplot(short_incubation, aes(x = onset_date)) +   geom_epicurve(fill = "coral") +   labs(title = "Short Incubation", x = NULL, y = "Cases") +   scale_y_epicurve() +   theme_minimal()  p2 <- ggplot(long_incubation, aes(x = onset_date)) +   geom_epicurve(fill = "skyblue") +   labs(title = "Long Incubation", x = "Date of Onset", y = "Cases") +   scale_y_epicurve() +   theme_minimal()  p1 / p2

code: # Hourly data for rapid outbreak investigation hourly_cases <- simulate_outbreak(   n = 15,   time_unit = "hourly",   exposure = "2024-06-01",   seed = 123 )  p1 <- ggplot(hourly_cases, aes(x = onset_time)) +   geom_epicurve(fill = "darkred") +   labs(title = "Hourly Epidemic Curve", x = "Time", y = "Cases") +   scale_y_epicurve() +   theme_minimal()  # Weekly aggregated data for surveillance weekly_cases <- simulate_outbreak(   n = 20,   time_unit = "weekly",   exposure = "2024-01-01",   seed = 456 )  p2 <- ggplot(weekly_cases, aes(x = onset_date)) +   geom_epicurve(fill = "forestgreen") +   labs(title = "Weekly Epidemic Curve", x = "Week", y = "Cases") +   scale_y_epicurve() +   theme_minimal()  p1 / p2

title: paulmisc: Epidemiological Visualization & SQL Tools
text: Add context epidemic curves event markers period shading:  interactive plotly timelines, see interactive epicurves vignette shows combine ggplot2 layers plotly annotations.
code: # Create an outbreak timeline outbreak_cases <- simulate_outbreak(n = 60, seed = 789)  ggplot(outbreak_cases, aes(x = onset_date)) +   geom_epicurve(fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.8) +   # Shade the likely exposure period   annotate_period(     date = as.Date("2024-05-28"),     end_date = as.Date("2024-06-02"),     label = "Likely exposure period",     fill = "yellow",     alpha = 0.25   ) +   # Mark when investigation started   annotate_event(     date = as.Date("2024-06-03"),     label = "Investigation\ninitiated",     colour = "darkgreen"   ) +   # Mark when source was identified   annotate_event(     date = as.Date("2024-06-07"),     label = "Source\nidentified",     colour = "red"   ) +   labs(     title = "Outbreak Timeline with Key Events",     x = "Date of Onset",     y = "Number of Cases"   ) +   scale_y_epicurve() +   theme_minimal()

code: annotate_event(   date,   label,   colour = "red",   color = NULL,   linetype = "dashed",   linewidth = 0.75,   label_y = Inf,   label_hjust = 0,   label_vjust = 0,   label_size = 3.5,   ... )  annotate_period(   date,   end_date,   label,   fill = "grey",   colour = NA,   color = NULL,   alpha = 0.3,   label_y = Inf,   label_hjust = 0.5,   label_vjust = 0,   label_size = 3.5,   ... )

title: Annotate epidemic curves with events and periods — annotate_epicurve
text: date Date POSIXct value event start period label Character string annotation label colour, color Colour line fill (American/British spelling accepted) linetype Line type event markers (default: "dashed") linewidth Width event line (default: 0.75) label_y Vertical position label (default: "top" events, "top" periods). Can numeric "top"/"bottom"/"middle". label_hjust Horizontal justification label (default: 0 events, 0.5 periods) label_vjust Vertical justification label (default: 1 events, 1 periods - labels hang top) label_size Text size label (default: 3.5) ... Additional arguments passed underlying geom end_date End date periods (required annotate_period()) alpha Transparency period shading (default: 0.3)

title: Epicurve geom: one square per case — geom_epicurve
text: geom_epicurve() draws classical epidemiological curve every individual case rendered small square stacked top others sharing date (binning unit x-axis). companion stat, stat_epicurve(), assigns case vertical stacking position within x-value bin.

title: Epicurve geom: one square per case — geom_epicurve
code: geom_epicurve(   mapping = NULL,   data = NULL,   stat = "epicurve",   position = "identity",   ...,   width = NULL,   height = 0.9,   max_stack = 20,   symbol = NULL,   symbol_size = 3,   na.rm = FALSE,   show.legend = NA,   inherit.aes = TRUE )  stat_epicurve(   mapping = NULL,   data = NULL,   geom = "rect",   position = "identity",   ...,   width = NULL,   height = 0.9,   max_stack = 20,   symbol = NULL,   symbol_size = 3,   na.rm = FALSE,   show.legend = NA,   inherit.aes = TRUE )

title: Epicurve geom: one square per case — geom_epicurve
text: mapping Set aesthetic mappings created ggplot2::aes(). data data displayed layer. stat statistical transformation use data; defaults "epicurve". position Position adjustment, defaults "identity". ... arguments passed ggplot2::layer(). width Numeric width case square x-axis units. NULL (default), automatically determines appropriate width based time unit: 0.9 daily Date data, 3600 seconds hourly POSIXct data, 6.3 weekly data, etc. Specify explicitly override auto-detection. height Numeric height case square y-axis units; defaults 0.9. Values 1 produce visible gaps stacked cases. max_stack Numeric threshold switching individual case squares column chart. maximum count x-value exceeds threshold, plot automatically displays column chart instead stacked squares. Set NULL always show squares (default: 20). symbol Character string specifying Unicode symbol emoji use instead squares (default: NULL squares). provided, case rendered specified symbol. Examples: "●" (bullet), "■" (square), "▲" (triangle), "♥" (heart), "😷" (face mask emoji). Ignored max_stack threshold exceeded (uses column chart instead). Can also mapped aesthetic different symbols per group. symbol_size Size symbols symbol used (default: 3). Adjust symbols appear large small relative plot. na.rm FALSE (default), missing values removed warning. show.legend Logical. layer included legends? inherit.aes FALSE, overrides default aesthetics rather combining . geom geometric object use; defaults "epicurve".

title: Epicurve geom: one square per case — geom_epicurve
code: library(ggplot2)  cases <- simulate_outbreak()  # Minimal epicurve (daily data) ggplot(cases, aes(x = onset_date)) +   geom_epicurve(fill = "steelblue") +   theme_minimal()   # Coloured by age group, faceted by setting ggplot(cases, aes(x = onset_date, fill = age_group)) +   geom_epicurve(colour = "grey20") +   facet_wrap(~ setting, ncol = 1) +   scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +   theme_bw()   # Hourly data (width auto-detects from POSIXct intervals) hourly_cases <- data.frame(   onset_time = as.POSIXct("2024-06-01 08:00:00") + 3600 * c(0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 3, 4),   case_id = 1:7 ) ggplot(hourly_cases, aes(x = onset_time)) +   geom_epicurve(fill = "darkred") +   theme_minimal() +   labs(title = "Hourly Epidemic Curve")   # Weekly data (width auto-detects from Date intervals) weekly_cases <- data.frame(   epi_week = as.Date("2024-01-01") + 7 * c(0, 1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 4),   case_id = 1:8 ) ggplot(weekly_cases, aes(x = epi_week)) +   geom_epicurve(fill = "forestgreen") +   theme_minimal() +   labs(title = "Weekly Epidemic Curve")   # Automatic column chart for large outbreaks (max_stack threshold) # When any date has > 20 cases, automatically switches to column chart large_outbreak <- data.frame(   onset_date = as.Date("2024-01-01") + sample(0:10, 150, replace = TRUE) ) ggplot(large_outbreak, aes(x = onset_date)) +   geom_epicurve(fill = "coral", max_stack = 20) +   theme_minimal() +   labs(title = "Large Outbreak (auto-switched to column chart)")   # Force square mode even for large counts by setting max_stack = NULL ggplot(large_outbreak, aes(x = onset_date)) +   geom_epicurve(fill = "coral", max_stack = NULL) +   theme_minimal() +   labs(title = "Large Outbreak (forced square mode)")   # Use symbols instead of squares cases_symbols <- simulate_outbreak(n = 30, seed = 999) ggplot(cases_symbols, aes(x = onset_date)) +   geom_epicurve(symbol = "●", symbol_size = 4, colour = "darkblue") +   theme_minimal() +   labs(title = "Epidemic Curve with Bullet Symbols")   # Use emoji symbols (requires font support) ggplot(cases_symbols, aes(x = onset_date, colour = sex)) +   geom_epicurve(symbol = "😷", symbol_size = 5) +   scale_colour_manual(values = c("Female" = "#D55E00", "Male" = "#0072B2")) +   theme_minimal() +   labs(title = "COVID-19 Cases with Face Mask Emoji")

what: Simulate onset dates for a point-source disease outbreak — simulate_outbreak
title: Simulate onset dates for a point-source disease outbreak — simulate_outbreak
text: Generates small, realistic line list single point-source outbreak. Incubation periods drawn log-normal distribution (classical choice many enteric respiratory pathogens), producing right-skewed onset distribution typical point-source events. handful categorical case attributes (age group, sex, outcome, setting) simulated alongside, resulting data frame can used demonstrate test plotting functions geom_epicurve().

title: Simulate onset dates for a point-source disease outbreak — simulate_outbreak
code: simulate_outbreak(   n = 20,   exposure = as.Date("2024-06-01"),   meanlog = 1.6,   sdlog = 0.45,   time_unit = c("daily", "hourly", "weekly"),   pattern = c("point_source", "continuous"),   date_range = 10,   seed = 42 )

title: Simulate onset dates for a point-source disease outbreak — simulate_outbreak
text: n Integer. Number cases simulate. Defaults 20. exposure Date (object coercible Date) giving common point-source exposure date. Defaults "2024-06-01". meanlog, sdlog Numeric. Parameters log-normal incubation period distribution log scale, passed stats::rlnorm(). median incubation period exp(meanlog) days, sdlog controls spread. Defaults (meanlog = 1.6, sdlog = 0.45) give median ~5 days moderate spread, typical many foodborne pathogens. quick-onset diseases like norovirus, try meanlog = 0.5 (median ~1.6 days). slow-onset diseases like hepatitis , try meanlog = 3 (median ~20 days). time_unit Character string specifying time resolution outbreak data. Options: "daily" (default, returns Date), "hourly" (returns POSIXct hour resolution), "weekly" (returns Date aggregated weeks). pattern Character string specifying outbreak pattern. Options: "point_source" (default, log-normal incubation single exposure) "continuous" (uniform distribution date range ongoing transmission). date_range Integer. continuous pattern, number days/hours/weeks cases uniformly distributed. Ignored point_source pattern. seed Optional integer used seed random number generator reproducibility. Use NULL leave RNG state untouched.

title: Simulate onset dates for a point-source disease outbreak — simulate_outbreak
text: data frame one row per case. daily/weekly data: columns case_id, onset_date, age_group, sex, outcome, setting. hourly data: onset_time instead onset_date.
